issues.description: The problem statement and UML describe a Stock class and require the SealSaloon.stock attribute to be of type Stock (and related static methods to operate on Stock). However, the template and the provided solution use an Inventory class that implements the stock functionality while Stock.java is empty. This mismatch between the expected Stock type and the actual Inventory type (and the empty Stock file) is structural and will confuse students about which class to implement and what the type of the stock attribute should be.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the naming and types consistent across the problem statement, template, and solution. Either: (A) update the problem statement and UML to refer to Inventory instead of Stock, or (B) rename Inventory.java to Stock.java (or provide a Stock class that delegates to Inventory) and update all references so SealSaloon.stock is of type Stock. Also ensure Stock.java in the template is populated (or removed if Inventory is intended) so students clearly know which class to implement/use.

issues.description: The problem statement and UML refer to a 'Stock' class as the saloon's inventory, but the provided codebase (template and solution) implements this concept as a class named 'Inventory'. Additionally, the template contains an empty Stock.java file. This mismatch (Stock vs Inventory) creates a mapping ambiguity for students: the exercises and UML expect operations and types on Stock, while the working implementation and examples use Inventory. Students may be unsure whether to modify Stock.java, Inventory.java, or both, and may waste time reconciling the two names.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the identifier for the inventory concept across all artifacts. Either rename the Inventory class/file to Stock (and update all references) so it matches the problem statement/UML, or update the problem statement and UML to consistently use 'Inventory' instead of 'Stock'. Also remove or implement the empty Stock.java in the template to avoid confusion (e.g., delete it or make it a thin alias/delegation to Inventory).
